item.title: One dead, 30 missing after ferry sinks off Vanuatu
item.description:
At least one person was killed and 30 are missing after a ferry sank off the coast of Vanuatu, the South Pacific nation’s government said on Sunday.
The vessel, MV Matui, had set sail on Friday with more than 40 passengers and crew from the island of Santo to Ambae island in very rough seas, but did not arrive.
Prime Minister Jotham Napat’s office said on Sunday morning that one dead body has been recovered, while 15 of those onboard have been “accounted for alive.”
The alarm was raised on Saturday afternoon when a diver working at a hotel on Santo saw a man floating in a life vest and pulled him to shore.
Hotel owner Ashley Beveridge told AFP he realized his employee was carrying a survivor from the missing boat, and someone in the restaurant alerted the authorities.
“He looked like he had been in the bathtub for 25 hours -- he was wrinkled up and white. He was cold,” Beveridge said in a telephone interview.
The survivor, Jeffson, said the boat sank on Friday morning.
“There was no rescue started until this guy got washed up on our beach -- lucky he got washed up in an inhabited area,” Beveridge said.
“He had gone all day and all night in the water.”
Beveridge said on Sunday afternoon: “At the last count it is 18 recovered and there is two or three dead so far.”
Cargo ship owners including a local politician, a local doctor with a plane and a private medical assistance vessel began their search on Saturday afternoon.
Survivors are being taken to the hospital on Santo Island, local media reported.
Napat’s office took over the maritime search on Sunday afternoon, after the prime minister earlier expressed frustration that he had been unable to reach senior officials.
In its Sunday statement, Napat’s office said “over 30 people remain missing at sea,” in addition to the one dead and the 15 “accounted for alive.”
“Our hearts and prayers are with the families who have lost loved ones. Search and rescue operations are continuing,” the statement read.
An investigation into potential negligence has been launched.
“This loss appears to be the result of strong winds and marine warnings not being heeded, and possibly of negligence including overloading of the vessel,” the statement added.
Beveridge, an Australian living in Vanuatu for eight years, said until Jeffson was discovered authorities had believed the ferry was adrift, and there was community frustration that the rescue effort took so long to get underway.
The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in Noumea, New Caledonia said it is assisting with the search, and a French Armed Forces aircraft was deployed on Sunday morning.
The center said 12 people were located on Sunday morning.
Matai Seremaiah, the member of parliament for Luganville who took part in the search aboard his family’s cargo vessel, said two survivors and one body had been discovered Sunday on Tutuba Island.

item.title: Indonesia says six killed, 130 missing after ferry capsizes off Java
item.description:
Rescuers in Indonesia said at least six people were killed and 130 others were missing on Sunday after a ferry sailing between the islands of Java and Borneo was hit by bad weather and capsized.
The Virgo Transport 8, carrying 243 passengers and crew, had lost contact with its shipping company early on Sunday after departing from Surabaya in East Java.
Basarnas, Indonesia’s national search and rescue agency, said in its latest update that six people were killed and 130 were missing. It said 107 people had been rescued.
There were 213 passengers and 30 crew members on board, the agency added.
Indonesian Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said the ship had capsized.
“From the information we received, based on helicopter surveillance... the ship capsized but has not sunk. As of 3pm (0700 GMT) it had not sunk yet, but it was capsized,” he said at a news conference in Banjarmasin.
Local search and rescue chief I Putu Sudayana earlier told AFP that the ship’s captain had reported to its owners before losing contact that the vessel was “tilting.”
Rescuers battled waves of up to 2.5 meters (8.2 feet) to reach the ferry, Sudayana told reporters.
“It is extremely risky for vessels. Even our Basarnas vessel, which is 40 meters long, is at great risk,” he said.
A Basarnas helicopter has joined the operation, he added.
The vessel’s last position had been detected in the Java Sea, around 150 kilometers (93 miles) from its destination.
Heri Purwanto, head of the Banjarmasin Sea Port Authority, said the ship, which was also carrying vehicles, lost contact at 2am on Sunday.
“We responded quickly to the incident report... Our main focus and top priority at this time is the safety of everyone on board the ship, and we are deploying a coordinated rescue operation,” Heri Purwanto said.
Rescue authorities have established a command center at the Banjarmasin port, with paramedics and ambulances on standby, an AFP reporter saw.
Dozens of relatives and friends of the passengers checked a whiteboard where the names of people rescued were being updated.
Jenah, 26, told AFP she came to the command post for information about her older brother.
“I am saddened and very shocked. Until now, I haven’t received any more information,” said Jenah, who like many Indonesians has only one name.
“He was travelling alone. I hope he survives. I couldn’t contact him since last night.”
Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia, an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that relies heavily on boat connections for daily transport and tourism.
Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.
On Monday, a speedboat carrying eight people, including five journalists working for local and international news agencies, went missing near a volcano, Mount Anak Krakatau, in Banten province. That search is ongoing.
The journalists were sent to cover the volcano’s eruption that paralyzed Jakarta’s main airport and several others.
Last month, a fire on board a ferry killed one person and left five others missing while 211 were rescued in the Lombok Strait off Indonesia’s Bali island.
The ferry had been heading from Bali to Lombok when it ran into trouble in the early hours of August 12.
In July, a ferry transporting more than 70 people sank while sailing near Selayar, a small island south of Sulawesi.

item.title: TikTok, IDLC launch program to empower Bangladeshi SMEs
item.description:
TikTok on Sunday launched TikTok Bazaar, a nationwide capacity-building program designed to equip small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Bangladesh with the digital marketing skills and capabilities needed to grow their businesses locally and internationally.
Implemented in partnership with IDLC Finance, the country’s leading NBFI, TikTok Bazaar aims to support up to 2,500 SMEs across the country through a combination of in-person workshops, advanced training clusters, online mentoring, and ongoing virtual support.
The program will help entrepreneurs move beyond traditional social commerce by using TikTok to reach wider audiences, strengthen their brands, and explore new business opportunities locally and internationally.
Additionally, the partnership will help expand entrepreneurs’ access to practical digital skills and introduce participating businesses to a broader digital ecosystem.
TikTok Bazaar responds to a significant opportunity within Bangladesh’s developing digital commerce ecosystem.
Many local entrepreneurs already use social media to promote and sell clothing, food, cosmetics, personal care products, handicrafts, accessories and more.
However, they often lack access to structured, practical performance marketing training, limiting their ability to optimize campaigns and drive sustainable business growth.
The program will help participating businesses develop practical skills in TikTok campaign planning, creative content production, account configuration, advertising optimization, and performance measurement.
Businesses with operational readiness will also receive guidance on reaching overseas customers and building export-oriented campaigns.
Ferdous Mottakin, head of public policy and government relations, South Asia, TikTok, said: "Digital creativity can be a powerful driver of business growth. In partnership with IDLC, we aim to provide SMEs with the knowledge, tools and support they need to turn creativity into measurable commercial opportunity through TikTok Bazaar, whether they are serving customers locally or introducing Bangladeshi products to audiences overseas."
“Digital inclusion is no longer optional for today’s SME businesses, and if they are based outside the larger markets like Dhaka, or Chattogram this becomes even more critical for their growth. Bangladesh has a very potential SME scenario; and from IDLC, we are putting our best efforts to upskilling local SME business owners through collaborating with partners like TikTok,” said Adnan Rashid, head of SME, IDLC Finance.
Through TikTok Bazaar, TikTok aims to help Bangladeshi entrepreneurs build more resilient businesses, connect with new customers, and participate more fully in the digital economy.
The initiative will help SMEs build confidence, expand their reach and pursue sustainable growth in both domestic and international markets.

item.title: Know groups and schedule as Bangladesh begin Asian Games women’s football campaign Monday
item.description:
Bangladesh will take part in the Asian Games women’s football competition for the second time after making their debut in the previous edition in China.
The Bengal Tigresses will begin their 2026 Asian Games campaign against Asian powerhouse North Korea at Nagai Stadium in Osaka on Monday.
They will then face another Asian giant, South Korea, at the same venue in their second group-stage match.
The 20th edition of the continental multi-sport competition is being held in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, with football matches taking place across several Japanese cities.
The women’s football competition will be staged in Osaka, Fukuroi, Gifu and Kariya, while the men’s event will be played in Osaka, Toyota, Nagoya and Kariya.
At the last Asian Games in 2023, Japan won the women’s football gold medal in Hangzhou, while the Republic of Korea clinched the men’s title.
The 12-team women’s competition, divided into three groups, will run from September 14 to October 2. The men’s competition, featuring 15 teams following Iraq’s withdrawal, will take place from September 15 to October 3.
Bangladesh have been drawn in Group F alongside the Republic of Korea, the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea and Myanmar.
The women in red and green, who made history by qualifying for the final round of the AFC Women’s Asian Cup 2026 in Australia in March, suffered an injury setback ahead of their Asian Games opener.
Defender Nabiran Khatun has been ruled out of the squad after sustaining a knee injury during a practice match in China last week.
Bangladesh head coach Peter Butler said the team’s strength lies in the players’ fighting mentality as they prepare for a challenging group stage.

item.title: Standard Chartered Bangladesh hosts inaugural financial markets leadership forum
item.description:
Standard Chartered Bangladesh recently convened the inaugural Financial Markets Leadership Forum for Financial Institution clients in Bangladesh.
The event brought together regulators and nearly 200 industry leaders from banks, financial institutions, and capital markets to share perspectives on the evolving financial markets landscape, regulatory leadership, market stability, and opportunities for sustainable growth and innovation in Bangladesh.
Discussions during the forum focused on how stronger risk management practices, deeper and more liquid markets, and the strategic use of technology and sustainable finance can help Bangladesh navigate global uncertainty and capture new opportunities.
Participants highlighted the critical role of robust market infrastructure, regulatory clarity, and collaboration in strengthening Bangladesh’s position within the global financial system.
The forum was graced by Masud Khan, chairman of the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission as chief guest, and Md Sarwar Hossain, deputy governor of Bangladesh Bank, as special guest.
Their presence underscored the importance of close and continuous engagement between regulators and market participants in building a robust, resilient, and future ready financial system.
“Bangladesh’s financial markets stand at a pivotal moment,” said Enamul Huque, CEO, Standard Chartered Bangladesh.
“By deepening market liquidity, strengthening risk management, and embracing digital and sustainable finance, we can unlock the next phase of growth for our economy. Standard Chartered is proud to convene this dialogue and to stand alongside our regulators and clients as a long-term partner in building a more resilient, inclusive, and future ready financial system. My sincere thanks to Masud Khan, chairman of the BSEC as chief guest; Md Sarwar Hossain, deputy governor of Bangladesh Bank, as special guest; to all speakers, panelists, clients and colleagues for their valuable insights and participation.”
On behalf of Standard Chartered Bangladesh, the Bank's CEO, Enamul Haque, delivered the opening remarks and head of markets and corporate sales Sabah Saleheen Azim moderated the event and panel discussion.
Other panelists and speakers include Mashrur Arefin, managing director, City Bank PLC; Mehdi Zaman, DMD and head of treasury, offshore banking and financial institutions, Eastern Bank PLC; and from Standard Chartered, Ashish Malik, head, Markets FI Sales South Asia; Himanshu Dhyani, head of FI, GCNA, & Head of BBD, GCNA South Asia, CIB FI BBD; and Nasreen Rehman, head of financial institutions, Bangladesh.

item.title: 'The Difficult Bride' wins independent critics’ award at Venice
item.description:
Bangladeshi filmmaker Rubaiyat Hossain’s “The Difficult Bride” has won the Independent Film Critics Award, Premio Bisato d’Oro, at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival ahead of the festival’s official awards ceremony.
The recognition adds to a landmark year for the film, which made history as the first Bangladeshi feature to compete in the Orizzonti Competition at the Venice Film Festival.
Set in contemporary Dhaka, “The Difficult Bride” follows Zaineen, a young bride-to-be whose body begins to transform as she undergoes beauty rituals and preparations for her wedding.
Blending feminist folk horror, body horror, and supernatural elements, the film examines how women’s bodies can become sites of family expectations, social control, and desire.
Hossain said the award was particularly meaningful because of the personal themes explored in the film.
“I made ‘The Difficult Bride’ from a very intimate place, thinking about the ways women learn to inhabit, discipline, and sometimes fear their own bodies,” she said. “To have the film recognized by independent critics in Venice is deeply meaningful to me.”
She added that she hopes the film will allow audiences to experience Bangladesh beyond its social realities through its folklore, imagination, darkness, and beauty.
The Bisato d’Oro is an independent critics’ prize associated with the Venice Film Festival and is separate from the official awards presented by the Biennale.
The film’s Venice selection had already attracted international attention, with critics highlighting its use of South Asian wedding rituals within a feminist folk-horror framework. IndieWire described the film as transforming South Asian wedding tropes into “feminist folk horror."
Produced by Francois D’Artemare, “The Difficult Bride” is an international co-production between Bangladesh, France, Germany, Norway, and Portugal. International sales are handled by Films Boutique.

item.title: I Am Not My Grades: The Hidden Toll of the A-Level System
item.description:
Around the same time last year, I was the centre of attention for the whole family. Achieving eight A*s in my O Levels was a big deal, something most people never expected from me. Although I was a bit disappointed about the single A in Computer Science, I was happy enough seeing my parents, grandparents, and teachers genuinely proud and satisfied. I was the success story of the batch, operating on a high that made the future look limitless.
Now, I am the center of pity.
Teachers tilt their heads with sympathetic smiles in the corridors, and relatives offer soft, comforting words, treating my AS Level results like a sudden bereavement.
I got a B in Further Mathematics, which was, quite frankly, a humbling slap in the face.
That single grade didn't just hurt my pride; it paralyzed my entire future.
Right now, my peers are living in the exciting world of top-tier university applications. I watch as friends refine their personal statements, draft college essays, and register for entrance tests.
They are locking in their predicted grades and preparing to hit submit for the October 15 Oxbridge deadline, or aiming for Early Decision slots at elite US universities.
Last year, everyone assumed I would be the first in line for those forms.
Today, I can’t even open the application portals. I am completely locked out of the early cycle, unable to apply anywhere because my grades are temporarily stuck in limbo.
Instead of moving forward, my life has been thrown into reverse. I am currently trapped in the exhausting nightmare of preparing for an October retake.
Balancing the relentless demands of new A2 coursework while re-studying the grueling concepts of Further Math feels virtually impossible.
My daily routine has dissolved into a blur of past papers, sleepless nights, and a constant, quiet panic.
I am trying to keep my head above water in current classes while desperately trying to repair the past, leaving zero hours to breathe, let alone draft university essays.
To go from being the kid everyone brags about to the kid everyone tries to console is a jarring shift. High expectations create a narrow window for success; anything less than perfection gets treated like a total collapse.
The pity, while well-intentioned, stings worse than anger. It serves as a daily, painful reminder of where I was supposed to be versus where I am standing right now, watching everyone else sprint ahead while I am forced to pause.
Yet, sitting at my desk late at night surrounded by notes I thought I had already put behind me, I am coming to terms with a hard truth. O Levels were smooth sailing, but this period is forcing me to figure out what I am actually made of.
Falling short doesn't erase my past achievements, nor does a delayed application deadline mean a ruined life.
The October session is going to be brutal, and missing out on early applications hurts. But learning how to fight through burnout, rebuild from a set-back, and pull myself out of the center of pity is the most important lesson I will take into adulthood.
Avranil Saha is an A2 Level student at St. Francis Xavier's Greenherald International School, Dhaka.

item.title: Salahuddin, IRI delegation discuss cybercrime, online bullying
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed on Sunday held a meeting with a delegation of the International Republican Institute (IRI), with discussions focusing on preventing cybercrime and online bullying, and the proposed Cyber Security (Amendment) Act 2026.
The courtesy meeting took place at the minister's office at noon.
The delegation was led by IRI Resident Program Director John Fluharty. Helen Jerin Khan, MP, IRI Technical Adviser Ruksana Haque, and young politicians and IRI trainees Chamon Faria and Mohammad Prince were also present.
During the meeting, Fluharty briefed the minister on IRI's ongoing programs aimed at developing youth leadership and promoting violence-free political practices.
He said young people and political activists in Bangladesh are currently facing harassment and defamation due to cyberbullying and organized disinformation.
Fluharty called for a consensus-based policy and legal protection for both the government and opposition parties in this regard.
The minister assured the delegation that the government is aware of citizens' freedom of expression and personal security.
“Under Article 39 of the Constitution, every citizen has the right to express opinions and engage in constructive criticism, subject to reasonable restrictions. However, constructive criticism is not the same as character assassination or abusive language for political purposes,” he said.
Salahuddin said the government has been seeking opinions from the international community, media personalities, senior editors and civil society stakeholders for the past two months as part of efforts to revise the proposed Cyber Security (Amendment) Act.
He said the main objectives of the law is to restore civility in the digital space, protect women and young people from cyberbullying and ensure professional protection for journalists while preventing any misuse of the law.
The minister said the government will welcome constructive recommendations from both international and local stakeholders to strengthen digital security and establish a violence-free political environment.
Additional Home Secretary (Political and Immigration Wings) Dr Ziauddin Ahmed and Joint Secretary of the Political-1 Branch Rebeka Khan, among others, attended the meeting.

item.title: Chief prosecutor: Threats to witnesses cannot obstruct tribunal proceedings
item.description:
International Crimes Tribunal Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam has said no one will be allowed to threaten or intimidate witnesses in crimes against humanity cases or obstruct judicial proceedings.
He made the remarks while responding to questions from journalists at his office on Sunday afternoon.
Asked about allegations that witnesses were being threatened by the accused in a crimes against humanity case over incidents in Chittagong, Aminul said he had received complaints in this regard.
He said law enforcement agencies had been instructed to take necessary measures to ensure the witnesses’ security.
“If there is evidence that anyone is threatening a witness in a case, legal action can be taken,” he said.
He, however, said threats and intimidation would not be allowed to disrupt the judicial process.
“No investigation or trial before this tribunal can be obstructed through intimidation or threats,” the chief prosecutor said. On a complaint filed by the family seeking justice for the murder of journalist couple Sagar Sarwar and Meherun Runi, Aminul said the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) was currently investigating the case.
He said Megh’s maternal uncle Roman had submitted a written application to the tribunal seeking its intervention.
“Their expectation is that we will also investigate the case or assist the PBI if we receive any information,” he said, adding that the application would be reviewed.
“If the matter does not fall under a widespread or systematic offence, we will inform them accordingly,” Aminul said.
He said anyone had the right to submit an application to the tribunal and that the family had exercised that right.
“The PBI investigation is ongoing. At this point, we consider the Sagar-Runi incident an individual murder case. We will examine whether it falls within the scope of a widespread or systematic offence,” he said.
He added that the application had been accepted, although it was not a matter of formally registering a case at this stage.

item.title: Yamal double helps Barca edge Levante thriller
item.description:
FBL-ESP-LIGA-LEVANTE-BARCELONA

Lamine Yamal struck twice to help Barcelona to an exciting 4-2 win at Levante on Sunday in La Liga, extending the Catalans' perfect start to the season.

Hansi Flick's side reestablished their three point lead over Real Madrid at the top of the table, after Los Blancos beat Rayo Vallecano on Saturday.

Xavi Espart opened the scoring for the champions in Valencia with Yamal netting the second and then scoring a penalty early in the second half.

Barca may have a 100 percent record so far from their five games but their defensive frailties were exposed as Ivan Romero and Roger Brugue pulled Levante back into the game in the final stages.

Substitute Karim Adeyemi made the game safe for Barca in stoppage time with a stunning solo goal, breaking through at pace and beating Mathew Ryan.

"It was not our best game of course. We had a great start. In the second half we struggled a little bit," Flick told reporters.

"We have to fight to improve. It's normal, we have situations we have to make better, much better. We'll tell the team and go on to the next match, but with the result I'm happy."

Barcelona defender Eric Garcia said that the team relaxed a bit in the second half and it nearly cost them.

"It was a hard game, we did make it harder for ourselves than it needed to be," Garcia told Movistar.

"But it has to teach us something -- if you give any opponent a bit of breathing room they get on top of you."

The Catalans came flying out of the blocks at the Cituat de Valencia stadium, where Levante were unbeaten in eight matches prior.

The visitors took the lead in the fifth minute, with Levante barely touching the ball before Barca defender Espart found the net.

Barca cut through the middle of Levante's team too easily and the 19-year-old finished from the edge of the box with the help of a slight deflection.

It was Espart's first goal for the club, with the young midfielder brought into the first team this season by Flick and deployed at left-back.

Levante responded with a spell of concerted pressure and Barca were fortunate to maintain their advantage.

Petar Ratkov could not get a proper shot away when well placed and Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia saved well from Brugue.

Levante soon came to regret those spurned chances when Raphinha created Barca's second for teenage star Yamal.

The Brazilian rounded goalkeeper Ryan and squared for Yamal to smash into the empty net in the 19th minute.

Between the afternoon summer heat and some heavy tackles, the pace of the game slowed.

Paying the penalty

Yamal claimed his second goal soon after the restart, winning and then converting a penalty.

The Spain winger was hacked down by Aissa Mandi and powered the resulting spot kick past Ryan for his seventh goal in four games across all competitions.

Levante could have pulled one back but Andreas Christensen cleared Romero's bobbling shot off the line.

The striker did get on the scoresheet when Espart gave the ball away with a loose pass towards Christensen, and Romero nipped in to strike.

Levante fans roared when Brugue capitalised on a Marc Bernal error, with Garcia saving his first shot but the striker able to nudge home the rebound.

However, former Borussia Dortmund winger Adeyemi ended the hosts' dreams of a point with a dynamic burst through the defence and then a cool finish to match.

Barcelona host promoted side Racing Santander on Wednesday, while Levante welcome Athletic Bilbao.

Earlier on Sunday, Celta Vigo were held to a 1-1 home draw by Malaga. Later, Diego Simeone's Atletico Madrid visit Real Sociedad and Getafe face Deportivo La Coruna.

item.title: NCP names mayoral candidates for Dhaka city polls
item.description:
The National Citizen Party (NCP) has announced its mayoral candidates for the two Dhaka city corporations.
The party named Nasiruddin Patwary as its candidate for Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) and Asif Mahmud for Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC).
Party convener and Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam announced the names on Sunday afternoon at an exchange meeting with potential councilor candidates from different wards of Dhaka South and North city corporations at the NCP office.
Earlier, the party had planned to field Asif Mahmud for Dhaka South and Ariful Islam Adib for Dhaka North.
At the meeting, Nahid Islam provided guidelines to potential councilor candidates from different wards of the 2 metropolitan areas. He instructed them to search for potential councilor candidates, identify ward-based civic problems, maintain regular contact with the families of July martyrs and those injured, and closely monitor sabotage activities by the ousted and absconding Awami League.
Isahak Sarkar and Ariful Islam Adib, conveners of the South and North metropolitan units respectively, along with leaders from different levels, were present at the meeting.

item.title: State Minister Tuku: Dengue crisis may worsen in coming months
item.description:
State Minister for Fisheries and Livestock Sultan Salauddin Tuku has said the ongoing dengue situation in Dhaka and other districts could take a more alarming turn over the coming months, urging citizens to remain vigilant from now.
"The risk of dengue may increase further in the coming months, so everyone needs to become aware from now," Tuku said while addressing a views exchange meeting with lawmakers and administration on the overall law and order situation and development activities in Dhaka district, held at the Dhaka Deputy Commissioner's conference room.
The state minister said public representatives, the administration and local residents must work together to combat dengue through cleanliness drives, destruction of mosquito breeding grounds and heightened public awareness.
On law and order in the capital, Tuku said maintaining law and order is not the administration's responsibility alone.
A safe and stable society, he said, can only be built through the coordinated efforts of political leadership, the administration, law enforcement agencies and the general public.
Noting that the government is working to keep the country's law and order situation normal while advancing development activities, he called for effective coordination among the district administration, police administration and public representatives, adding that obstacles to development work must be identified and addressed alongside maintaining law and order.
He stressed the need for special surveillance to prevent various criminal activities in the capital and its surrounding areas, particularly in crime-prone zones, calling for increased law enforcement activity and greater political and social awareness in those areas.
Describing drugs as a major threat to society that is drawing in people from all walks of life, Tuku said the administration, public representatives and social organisations must play a more active role in curbing the spread of narcotics.
Addressing government officials, the state minister said that as state functionaries, they must carry out their duties giving top priority to public welfare and state interests, stressing that all administrative activities should be conducted in the interest of the state and the people, not any individual or group.
The meeting was chaired by Dhaka Deputy Commissioner Farida Khanom. State Minister for the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain attended as special guest.
Also present were Chief Whip of the Opposition Nahid Islam, Dhaka-12 MP Saiful Alam Khan Milon, reserved women's seat MP Ferdousi Ahmed, Superintendent of Police Shamima Parveen, representatives of various law enforcement agencies, local government officials, public representatives and members of the district law and order committee.

item.title: Minister: No child to be deprived of education due to financial hardship
item.description:
Food Minister Afroza Khanam Rita on Sunday said the government is giving due importance to ensuring that no child is deprived of education due to financial hardship.
“Government assistance and various welfare programs will continue in the future to ensure educational opportunities for children from poor and disadvantaged families,” she said.
She made the remarks while addressing a function to distribute school uniforms among students at Betila Government Primary School as the chief guest.
The minister said ensuring quality education and necessary facilities for students is essential to building an educated, humane and discrimination-free society. The present government is working to establish a social and humane state, she added.
As part of these efforts, various programs are being implemented to encourage students in their studies, provide educational materials and facilitate their education, the minister said.
Afroza said improvements in the quality of education would accelerate the country’s progress. Today’s students will play an important role in running the country in the future. Therefore, creating a quality educational environment and ensuring conditions conducive to the development of their intellect and creativity are important responsibilities of the state, she added.
The food minister urged the students to attend school regularly and study attentively.
She also called upon teachers to teach with sincerity and responsibility while helping develop the students’ moral and humanitarian values.
Deputy Commissioner of the district Nazmun Ara Sultana chaired the program. Police Super Mohammad Sarwar Alam, relevant district and upazila-level officials, local leaders, teachers, guardians and students were, among others, present.
Later, the Betila Union BNP and its affiliated and associate organizations organized a mass reception for the food minister on the same school ground. Syed Maksudul Hasan Chowdhury presided over the reception.

item.title: ACC probes new allegations against Asif Mahmud
item.description:
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has decided to add a new set of allegations against former adviser Asif Mahmud to its ongoing inquiry into alleged financial transactions involving appointments and postings, commissions from development projects and tenders, bribery and money laundering.
ACC Deputy Director and Public Relations Officer Aktarul Islam disclosed the information at a press conference on Sunday.
Aktarul Islam said the new application contains allegations of irregularities and financial transactions involving the appointment of an administrator to Dhaka North City Corporation, the posting of deputy commissioners (DCs) in different districts, tender processes at Dhaka South City Corporation and other agencies, and development projects under the Ministry of Local Government.
According to the application submitted to the ACC, about Tk 60cr allegedly changed hands in the appointment of an administrator to Dhaka North City Corporation, while Tk 2cr to Tk 10cr per person was allegedly transacted in the posting of DCs in 36 districts.
Aktarul Islam said the allegations are being investigated.
The application also alleges that while Asif Mahmud was responsible for the Ministry of Local Government, he received commissions ranging from 10% to 30% from tenders for various development projects.
It also alleges his involvement in irregularities in tender processes at Dhaka South City Corporation, Narayanganj City Corporation and Comilla City Corporation.
The application further alleges that a large amount of money was embezzled by increasing the costs of rural infrastructure development and bridge construction projects under the Ministry of Local Government.
It also alleges an unusual increase in the cost of the 3rd phase of the Dhaka Water Supply and Sewerage Authority’s Sayedabad Water Treatment Plant project and an increase of nearly Tk 1,200cr in the cost of the Sheikh Russel Mini Stadium project to allegedly misappropriate money.
The application also contains allegations of transactions involving crores of taka in various appointments, transfers and promotions under the Ministry of Youth and Sports.
It alleges that Tk 10cr was taken as a bribe in exchange for appointing Abdus Salam as managing director of Dhaka Water Supply and Sewerage Authority, Tk 52cr was paid as a bribe for appointing former Local Government Engineering Department (LGED) chief engineer Md Abdur Rashid Khan, and Tk 65cr was transacted to appoint Abdul Latif Khan as chief executive officer of Gazipur City Corporation.
The application also raises allegations concerning Asif Mahmud’s lifestyle and acquisition of assets abroad. It claims that he regularly visited 5-star hotels, lived in a luxurious flat, used expensive cars and traveled by helicopter, resulting in the misuse of state funds.
It further alleges that land was purchased in Portugal, investments were made in a company in Dubai and money was deposited in Swiss banks with funds allegedly acquired through corruption.
The application claims that Tk 4,500cr was siphoned off to Dubai, Tk 3,000cr to Singapore, Tk 2,000cr to Australia and Tk 1,500cr to Switzerland, where assets were purchased and investments were made in various businesses.
It also alleges that money was laundered abroad through the husbands of 2 sisters and a nephew.
The ACC said the figures concerning money laundering and claims about assets are allegations made by the applicant. Their veracity is being verified through the inquiry.
The application also mentions an allocation of Tk 453cr for Asif Mahmud’s home upazila of Muradnagar under a rural infrastructure development project. The complainant claims the process of allocation and receipt of the funds under the project is questionable.
It also alleges that Asif Mahmud’s father Billal Hossain and his assistant private secretary (APS) Moazzem Hossain controlled a syndicate of contractors and collected money by influencing the local administration.
His personal officer (PO) Mahfuzul Alam Bhuiyan has also been accused of lobbying for bribery transactions and abusing power.
ACC Public Relations Officer Aktarul Islam said an inquiry into allegations of corruption and irregularities against Asif Mahmud had already been ongoing. He said the new allegations would be attached to the previous documents and investigated.
On September 2, ACC official Akhtarul Islam said at a press conference that the commission had found “initial evidence” of allegations of irregularities in transfers, appointments and promotions involving former adviser Asif Mahmud .
Following those remarks, the issue was widely circulated in various media outlets and on social media.
Asif Mahmud held a press conference that day to protest the allegations. On Thursday, Supreme Court lawyer Muhammad Rafiqul Islam Joni sent a notice to the ACC on his behalf.
The National Citizens Party (NCP) confirmed the matter in a statement sent to the media on Friday.
On the next working day, the ACC announced that it had received new allegations against Asif Mahmud and would investigate them.

item.title: DNCC fines Tk 1.77 lakh over Aedes larvae in Dhaka homes
item.description:
The Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) has realised Tk1,77,500 in fines from 28 cases after Aedes mosquito larvae were found in several households across various areas under its jurisdiction.
DNCC executive magistrates conducted mobile court drives in different areas on Sunday as part of a three-month-long mosquito eradication program, imposing the fines after detecting Aedes larvae on the premises of various homes.
The cases were filed in Mirpur-10, Rupnagar, Uttar Pallabi, Agargaon, Uttara Nikunjo and Baridhara areas, DNCC said.
The mobile courts were led by DNCC-appointed executive magistrates Atish Darshi Chakma, SM Rasel Islam Noor, Shariful Alam Tanvir, Pramotha Ranjan Ghatak and Dedarul Islam.
The drive comes under a three-month campaign announced by the Prime Minister on National Dengue Prevention Day.

item.title: Hajj-2027 registration ends on Sept 24
item.description:
The registration process for the 2027 Hajj will end on September 24 this year, with no scope for an extension, according to a notification issued by the Ministry of Religious Affairs.
As per instructions from the Saudi government, immediately after the registration process ends, the final number of Hajj pilgrims from Bangladesh will be communicated to the Saudi authorities.
Based on the final number of pilgrims, necessary activities, including remittance of funds for the Saudi phase, medical checkups, fitness certificates, vaccination, and training programs, will be carried out.
Bangladesh’s Hajj quota for 2027 is 78,500 pilgrims. As of September 9, 2026, a total of 3,741 pilgrims have registered, including 1,065 through the government channel and 2,676 through the private channel.
All concerned have been requested to complete registration within the stipulated deadline of September 24 to ensure their participation in the 2027 Hajj in accordance with the instructions of the Saudi government.
The registration process for Hajj 2027 began on July 27 this year.

item.title: PM for reducing import dependence by boosting farm production
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday stressed the need to reduce Bangladesh’s dependence on imports of agricultural and food products by increasing domestic production of crops that can be grown in the country.
He also asked officials of the Ministry of Agriculture to take effective measures to boost the production of locally viable agricultural commodities, while ensuring food security and making farming more productive and profitable, said a release issued by the PM’s Press Wing.
The prime minister gave the directives at a meeting with officials of the ministry at its conference room in the Bangladesh Secretariat in the afternoon.
He directed officials to focus not only on increasing agricultural productivity but also on reducing farmers’ production costs and ensuring fair prices for their produce.
“We must gradually reduce our dependence on imports of agricultural and food products that can be produced domestically. To this end, we need to put greater emphasis on increasing domestic production by quickly taking research findings, improved varieties, modern technologies, irrigation facilities and mechanization to farmers,” Tarique Rahman said.
Earlier, the prime minister walked from his office to the agriculture ministry and took the stairs instead of using the lift to reach the ministry’s conference room.
At the meeting, officials presented the overall situation of the agriculture sector, ongoing activities of the ministry and its plans.
The ministry informed the meeting that mustard production has increased significantly as part of efforts to reduce dependence on imported edible oil.
Mustard production rose from 8.24 lakh tonnes in 2021-22 to 15.34 lakh tonnes in 2024-25 and 15.41 lakh tonnes in 2025-26.
The meeting was also informed of initiatives to increase onion production and storage capacity. “Measures include introducing air-flow technology for onion storage at farmers’ level and expanding summer onion varieties.”
The ministry is also working to expand climate-resilient crop varieties tolerant to salinity, drought and waterlogging at the field level.
Highlighting progress in agricultural research, officials said a total of 1,090 crop varieties have so far been developed, including 155 rice varieties.
More than 1,000 agricultural technologies have also been developed, according to the presentation.
The meeting stressed greater emphasis on agricultural mechanization to reduce labour and production costs while increasing productivity.
The government is working to increase domestic production of agricultural machinery and make equipment such as combine harvesters, reapers and rice transplanters available to farmers at affordable prices.
The expansion of solar-powered irrigation was also discussed. There are currently 2,617 solar irrigation systems in the country, and expanding renewable energy-based irrigation could help reduce farmers’ irrigation costs and dependence on conventional fuels, officials said.
The meeting also reviewed the Farmers’ Card program aimed at ensuring direct delivery of government support to farmers.
The agriculture ministry has set a target of bringing 43 lakh farmers under the card program in the 2026-27 fiscal year. Preparations are underway to distribute cards to around 1.10 lakh farmers in the first phase, the meeting was informed.
The meeting also discussed canal excavation, tree plantation, and storage and marketing of farm produce.

item.title: Ten rescued after boat capsizes in Padma, including 20-day-old baby
item.description:
A 20-day-old baby was among 12 people swept into the Padma River after a boat capsized in Chapainawabganj on Saturday, with 10 Bangladeshis later rescued by India's Border Security Force (BSF) and one person still missing.
The boat capsized around 5:30pm while travelling from Bakherali to Johurpur Belpara in Chapainawabganj Sadar as the river became rough. The baby, Tanisha, was travelling in her mother Tania Khatun's arms when the boat sank and all 12 people on board fell into the water.
Photo: Dhaka Tribune
Md Wasim, 23, managed to swim to the shore, while the remaining 11 passengers went missing.
Amid the strong current and storm, the passengers tried to stay afloat by holding onto the boat’s wooden floor, sacks, floating pieces of wood, paddles and other objects.
Tania Khatun held Tanisha tightly, but at one point the strong current pulled the baby from her arms. Tania later found Tanisha underwater and held her tightly again.
Tanisha’s maternal grandfather Ibrahim also swam while holding the baby above the water with one hand.
After floating in the water for around 1 hour and 20 minutes, the current carried them towards Indian waters. BSF members spotted 10 Bangladeshis, including Tanisha, and went to rescue them in a speedboat before taking them to the riverbank.
At the time of the rescue, 20-day-old Tanisha was almost unresponsive after swallowing water while being held by her mother. BSF members quickly took her to a local medical centre, where doctors examined her and said she was healthy.
The incident occurred while the group was travelling from Bakherali in Chapainawabganj Sadar to Johurpur Belpara. Tanisha is the daughter of Md Sohel and Tania Khatun of Johurpur Belpara in Sadar upazila.
Shariful Islam, subedar of the Bakher Ali Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) camp, said rescuers told him that Tania had been holding Tanisha tightly after the boat sank.
He said: “They floated by holding onto the boat’s rice husk, paddle and wooden floor. At one point, the strong current pulled the child from her mother’s hand and she sank into the water. Later, Tania Khatun found her and held her tightly again.”
Shahidul Islam, company commander of Faridpur Border Outpost (BOP), said Tanisha’s maternal grandfather knew how to swim, while the women stayed afloat by holding onto the boat’s wooden floor, paddles and sacks.
He said: “They remained floating in the water for more than an hour.”
Rabiul Islam Rabu, member of Ward 8 of Narayanpur Union Parishad, said Tania initially held Tanisha tightly, but the strong current and storm caused the baby to slip from her arms and sink.
He said Tania later found Tanisha and held her above the water with her legs. Seeing the baby in distress, her grandfather Ibrahim held her above the water with 1 hand while swimming to survive.
Rabiul Islam Rabu said they remained in the water for around 1 hour and 20 minutes before BSF members rescued them.
Shyamalal Mondal, a resident of Taranagar in Lalbagh police station area of Murshidabad district, was present on the Indian side when the BSF rescued the Bangladeshis.
He said BSF members rescued the Bangladeshis and took them to the riverbank. He added that 20-day-old Tanisha was almost unresponsive at the time and that BSF members immediately took her to a local medical center, where doctors said she was healthy.
Lieutenant Colonel Kazi Mostafizur Rahman, commander of BGB’s 53 Battalion, said members of the BSF’s 71 Battalion Khandua Camp rescued the Bangladeshis with a speedboat on Saturday night.
He said the BSF handed over the 10 rescued Bangladeshis to the BGB that night, after which the BGB released them into the custody of their relatives.
Kazi Mostafizur Rahman said 9 of the 10 rescued Bangladeshis, including Tanisha, returned home that night in healthy condition.
At around 5pm on Saturday, a motorized boat carrying 12 passengers left Alimnagar Ghat in the Bakherali area for Johurpurtek village. The boat sank in the Padma River on the way.
At around 5:50pm, the company commander of the 71 Battalion BSF’s Khandua Camp informed the BGB about the boat sinking. He said the BSF had rescued 10 Bangladeshis alive, including 4 men, 3 women and 3 children.
The Chapainawabganj Battalion, 53 BGB, then took steps to bring them back to Bangladesh. At 9:55pm, a company commander-level flag meeting was held between the commander of Faridpur BOP and the commander of the Khandua BSF Camp.
Following the meeting, the 10 rescued Bangladeshis were brought back to Bangladesh. They were later handed over to their close relative, Md Ismail Hossain, in the presence of local public representatives.
The BGB said all the rescued people were in good health.
The rescued people were Md Russell, 26; Md Ibrahim, 50; Sowdagar, 40; Md Ibrahim, 60; Sakhina, 45; Nilufta, 35; Tania, 22, and her 20-day-old daughter; Sanaullah, 9; and Al Amin, 9.
All of them are from Johurpur (Bokaripara) village in Chapainawabganj.
Meanwhile, Md Mostafa, 60, son of late Altab Hossain, from the same village, remains missing. Search and rescue operations are continuing to locate him.

item.title: The RYZE of Bangladesh’s first AI Hub
item.description:
Artificial Intelligence has become deeply entwined within education, the arts, wellbeing, and everyday life. Consequently, access to different AI tools has become a daily requirement and an important part of the user experience. However, using multiple platforms simultaneously can be a hassle; switching between apps, managing separate subscriptions, and dealing with international payments.
Banglalink took the step towards simplifying AI access, bringing together multiple leading Artificial Intelligence models within its AI-powered digital lifestyle brand, RYZE. Incorporating ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Claude and Gemini within one interface, RYZE’s aim is to simplify access to advanced AI tools for everyday users, students, and professionals.
The RYZE AI Hub was initially soft launched in January this year during a freshers’ orientation programme at BRAC University by Banglalink’s CEO, Johan Buse. It was officially launched in April, marking its wider availability and giving users the chance to select models suited to different tasks, whether writing, research or other activities.
The focus on practical skills and employability has also brought international recognition. RYZE received the AI Innovation Award at the Global Conference on AI Leadership and Flagship Prestige Awards 2026 for its contribution to advancing AI solutions aimed at improving young people's skills and employability. The recognition came within the same year as the AI Hub’s commercial launch.
RYZE’s access model is also different from quintessential subscription approaches. Users get access to premium AI models by purchasing tokens and using them according to requirements rather than taking separate monthly subscriptions. The hassle of payment through dollar endorsed credit card is also removed as users are allowed to pay via local mobile financial services. Moreover, RYZE is not limited to users of one mobile network; it is a telco-agnostic platform that can be accessed by users across networks.
Users receive free 10,000 tokens upon signing up and do so each month for basic use. Additional tokens are available upon purchasing RYZE’s In-App Packs- Core, Pro, Max and Ultra. These packs offer 100,000, 210,000, 575,000, and 1,250,000 tokens respectively, each valid for 30 days.
For users in Bangladesh, the payment mechanism is another practical consideration, reflective of Banglalink’s commitment to care.
Access to many international digital services can be complicated by the need for an internationally enabled credit or debit card. Along with traditional payment methods, RYZE also allows users to purchase tokens through local mobile financial services such as bKash or Nagad.
As AI becomes increasingly relevant to learning and professional life, the evolution of platforms like RYZE suggests that the next question for Bangladesh may not simply be whether people can use AI, but how easily they can access the tools they need.

item.title: Harun’s family receives PM’s gift 12 years after his death
item.description:
More than 12 years after Jubo Dal leader Mohammad Harunur Rashid was killed in police firing in Feni, his family has finally received a new home.
BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi handed over the keys to the newly built house to Harunur’s family at Jagatjibanpur in Farhadnagar Union of the district on Sunday. His wife, Bibi Zohra, daughter Majeda Akter and son Touhidul Islam received the keys.
According to district BNP sources, Harunur was killed in police firing on December 4, 2013, amid tensions surrounding a BNP-led programme in support of a hartal on Shaheed Shahidullah Kaiser Road in Feni town. He was then vice-president of the Farhadnagar Union Jubo Dal.
After his death, his wife and children endured years of hardship, including uncertainty over their livelihood and housing.
The new house was built in Jagatjibanpur under an initiative of “Amra BNP Poribar” to rehabilitate the family, following instructions from Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. Construction began on April 12.
Speaking at the key handover ceremony, Ruhul Kabir Rizvi accused the previous Awami League government of enforced disappearances and killings.
“Sheikh Hasina did not hesitate to kill anyone to consolidate power. Enforced disappearances and killings continued for 17 years,” he said.
Local BNP leaders recalled Harunur’s political contributions and pledged to continue supporting his family.
The family expressed relief after finally receiving a secure home following years of housing difficulties, though the loss of their husband and father continues to leave a deep void in their lives.
After the ceremony, Rizvi visited Harunur’s grave and inaugurated the nameplate of the new house.

item.title: Government primary schools in Dhaka face enrolment decline
item.description:
On a school day, rows of empty benches outnumbered students at Swamibag Government Primary School in Dhaka, where only a few children were present during scheduled class hours.
At around 10am, three children were seen sitting in one classroom without a teacher. By around 1pm, the few students who remained had left, saying classes were over.
On another day, five students were present. However, government records show that the school has 58 students and 5 teachers.
The contrast between official records and what is visible inside classrooms is not limited to one school.
Over three days, Dhaka Tribune visited several government primary schools in Dhaka’s Sutrapur area, including Government Colony Primary, Swamibag Primary, Bongobashi Government Primary, Muslim Government and Narinda primary schools, at different times between 10am and noon.
Photo: Asiful Islam Rifat/Dhaka Tribune
The visits found classrooms with very few students, aging infrastructure, stagnant water, unclean surroundings, and limited space for children to play.
The gap between official data and ground reality extends to several other government primary schools in the area, including Bangla Bazar, Bongobashi, Muslim and Wari Mohila Somity primary schools.
Sutrapur Thana has 48 government primary schools, 322 working teachers, and 8,274 enrolled students.
Data shows low enrolment at several institutions. Muslim Government Primary School has 23 enrolled students for 4 teachers, Bongobashi Government Primary School lists 26 students for 3 teachers, Nobendro Boshak Lane Government Primary School has 32 students; and Narinda Mohila Somity Government Primary School reports 40 students.
However, the figures do not tell the whole story.
At Swamibag Government Primary School, official records list 58 students and five working teachers against six approved posts. Government data also shows that the school has nine classrooms, three toilets and a safe drinking water source.
During two separate visits, however, only three and five students, respectively, were seen at the school. Some classrooms were covered in dust, while waterlogging made parts of the school unsuitable for classes.
Photo: Asiful Islam Rifat/Dhaka Tribune
Addressing the discrepancy, Samina Yasmin, headteacher of Swamibag Government Primary School, said: “We have continuously informed the senior authorities about the structural issues at the school. They are well aware of the issue. Our teachers repeatedly encourage students to attend school and communicate with parents, but many children attend for a few days before becoming irregular again.”
She defended the teaching staff while acknowledging the attendance problems.
“We take classes regularly. But when there are no students, what classes can we take?” she added.
Kishori Rani Biswas, headteacher of Bongobashi Government Primary School, said: “Since I joined the school, I have tried my best to improve the situation. Currently, 33 students are enrolled here. We are continuously working to gradually increase the number of students.”
The problem is not limited to attendance. Plaster on the entrance walls was peeling off, revealing damp and weathered brickwork. The narrow passage leading inside was littered with debris and stagnant water.
Broken bricks, rubbish and stagnant water were visible in different areas of the premises. Moss had accumulated along parts of the boundary wall and in narrow spaces behind classrooms.
Classrooms were covered in dust and contained only a few broken benches and a fractured wallboard.
A significant portion of the school premises was waterlogged, with dark, dirty rainwater standing for extended periods. The stagnant water was accompanied by mosquitoes.
Photo: Asiful Islam Rifat/Dhaka Tribune
The surroundings of school equipment also appeared poorly maintained.
Similar problems were observed at Government Colony Primary School and most of the other schools visited in the area. In several places, aging buildings, limited open space and poor cleanliness were visible.
For many families, government primary schools remain an affordable option. But parents interviewed during the field visits said low cost alone was no longer enough to convince them to choose these schools.
Subhan Rahman, a guardian of two children, said the facilities and classroom environment were not satisfactory.
“The facilities are not very good. Classes are also not always held properly. That is why many people are not interested in sending their children here,” he said.
Farida Yasmin pointed to another problem, describing a cycle in which declining attendance further weakens the school environment.
“Classes are not always held regularly, and the infrastructure is also unsatisfactory. Besides, it creates a cycle. There are fewer students, so there is less activity in the classroom. Again, because the environment is not good, new students do not come,” she said.
Sharmin Sultana, a resident of the area, has not sent either of her two children to a government primary school. Instead, both attend a private institution.
For her, the decision was not simply about academic considerations.
“The school has transport and other facilities, which is important for working mothers. I don’t have to worry about taking my children to and from school,” she said.
“Private institutions follow a more up-to-date curriculum and provide greater individual attention to students,” she added.
Highlighting the systemic nature of the issue, educationist Prof Dr Manzoor Ahmed said affluent and middle-class urban families have long shifted away from government primary institutions.
Emphasizing that physical access alone cannot sustain enrollment without quality and safety, he said: “Dilapidated infrastructure, teacher shortage, security concerns, teaching methods, lack of play areas, and the absence of individualized learning support are driving parents away from government primary schools.”
Commenting on the structural deficiencies, Nahida Sultana, assistant thana education officer (ATEO) of Sutrapur, told Dhaka Tribune: “We are aware of the infrastructural issues in several schools under our jurisdiction. We have documented these concerns and submitted requests for necessary allocations to the higher authorities. Once funds are sanctioned, renovation and infrastructure improvement works will begin.”
She acknowledged administrative shortages, saying: “Some of the schools lack headteachers and assistant headteachers.”
She added: “Although student numbers are low due to parental reluctance, we are actively working to raise awareness among them. We are conducting cluster-based monitoring and submit weekly reports. If any teacher is found negligent in performing their classroom duties upon investigation, strict action will be taken.”
At a recent press conference, State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj said monitoring should not rely only on administrative reports and paperwork but should be based on actual results. On the declining attendance of students, Bobby Hajjaj told Dhaka Tribune: “We are trying to understand and meet the needs of parents and students and take measures accordingly. Government facilities are meant for the people. Our effort will be to understand what people want and find ways to meet those needs. If we fail to meet their needs, government primary schools will eventually be closed."
Asked about the government’s plans for the schools’ infrastructure, he said: “Yes, I am aware of the condition of the buildings. We are working to modernize these buildings, and hopefully, the work will begin by the end of this year or early next year.”
Educationists say government primary schools remain one of the few affordable avenues for formal education for many low-income families in Dhaka. If these institutions continue to lose students while private alternatives expand, the issue could affect access to affordable and equitable education in the capital.

item.title: Another train to be added on Dhaka–Cox’s Bazar route
item.description:
The railway authorities have taken an initiative to introduce another train on the Dhaka–Cox’s Bazar route. The Mahanagar Express, which currently operates on the Dhaka–Chattogram route, is being extended to the tourist city of Cox’s Bazar. Railway officials said the train may start operating up to Cox’s Bazar from the first week of October.

Although trains currently run from Dhaka to Cox’s Bazar, they do not stop anywhere along the route except Chattogram. Local residents and influential politicians have long been pressing for the trains to stop at various stations between Dhaka and Chattogram. The railway authorities have taken the initiative to extend the Mahanagar Express to Cox’s Bazar, giving passengers from those stations the opportunity to travel directly to the tourist city.

On 1 August, Railway Minister Habibur Rashid visited the Chattogram–Cox’s Bazar railway route. During the visit, he told journalists that plans were under way to increase the number of trains operating between Dhaka and Cox’s Bazar and between Chattogram and Cox’s Bazar in response to passenger demand.

Durga Puja: Special train to run on Dhaka-Cox’s Bazar route during holidays

He said there were currently four pairs of trains operating to Cox’s Bazar from Dhaka and Chattogram, and the plan was to increase the number to five pairs. Preparations were being made to achieve this, he said.

Sujit Biswas, chief commercial manager of the Eastern Railway, told Prothom Alo that there was strong passenger demand for the Cox’s Bazar route. In response to that demand, the Mahanagar Express operating on the Dhaka–Chattogram route was being extended to Cox’s Bazar.

Preparations were under way to launch the service from the first week of October. This would allow passengers to travel to the tourist city more comfortably and safely, while also increasing railway revenue, he said.

At present, two pairs (four trains) of non-stop intercity trains operate between Dhaka and Cox’s Bazar, while another two pairs (four trains) operate between Chattogram and Cox’s Bazar.

According to Railway Working Time Table-54 (WTT), the Mahanagar Express currently leaves Kamalapur station in Dhaka for Chattogram at 9:20 pm and arrives in Chattogram at 3:30 am. After leaving Kamalapur, the train stops at 12 stations, including the airport, where passengers can board and get off.

Apart from the airport, the Mahanagar Express stops at Narsingdi station in Narsingdi ; Bhairab Bazar station in Kishoreganj; Ashuganj, Brahmanbaria, Akhaura and Kasba stations in Brahmanbaria; Cumilla, Laksam and Nangalkot stations in Cumilla; Feni station in Feni; and Kumira station in Chattogram.

As there are no direct trains from these districts to Cox’s Bazar, passengers have to travel to the tourist city by road. If the Mahanagar Express is extended to Cox’s Bazar, passengers from these areas will be able to travel there directly by train.

Railway officials said the Mahanagar Express timetable would be revised once it begins operating to Cox’s Bazar. Under the proposed schedule, the train would leave Kamalapur in Dhaka at 8:30 pm and arrive in Cox’s Bazar at 6:00 am. The return train would leave Cox’s Bazar for Dhaka at 9:00 am. The journey would take around nine and a half hours each way.

The Cox’s Bazar Express, which currently operates on the Dhaka–Cox’s Bazar route, leaves Kamalapur at 11:00 pm and arrives in Cox’s Bazar at 7:20 am. The Tourist Express leaves Kamalapur at 6:15 am and reaches Cox’s Bazar at 2:40 pm.

A senior railway official told Prothom Alo that preparations were under way to operate the Mahanagar Express from Dhaka to Cox’s Bazar. The authorities were assessing what obstacles or problems might arise from extending the service to Cox’s Bazar. They were also considering how cleaning and maintenance of the train would be managed in Cox’s Bazar.

Old coaches on the Chattogram–Cox’s Bazar route

Meanwhile, even as preparations are under way to extend the Mahanagar Express from Dhaka to Cox’s Bazar, the process of introducing better-quality coaches, including air-conditioned (AC) coaches, on intercity trains operating on the Chattogram–Cox’s Bazar route has stalled.

Two pairs of intercity trains currently operate on the Chattogram–Cox’s Bazar route. All four trains are operated using a single rake—a combination of an engine and multiple coaches. As a result, the schedule is frequently disrupted. Passengers also suffer because of delays.

Passengers complain that although demand on the route has increased, all the coaches on the trains are old and of poor quality. Many passengers, in particular, are losing interest in travelling by train on this route because there are no AC coaches or cabin facilities. As the tourism-dependent route lacks quality services, its potential to generate revenue is also not being fully utilised.

According to data from the railway’s transport department, the Saikat and Probal Express each operate with 16 coaches. There had been plans to replace the old coaches and add one AC cabin, one non-AC cabin, three AC chair coaches (Snigdha), eight Shovon chair coaches, one power car and two guard brakes to each train. Each train has around 750 seats.

Railway officials said there was currently no possibility of replacing the coaches on the existing trains with better-quality coaches, including AC coaches. The coaches may be replaced when new coaches are imported, they said.

item.title: This year I deserve Ballon d'Or: Barca's Yamal
item.description:
SOCCER-SPAIN-VAL-BAR/

Lamine Yamal believes he and Kylian Mbappe are the two best players in the world and said he deserves to win the 2026 Ballon d'Or after a trophy-laden year with Barcelona and Spain.

"For me, Mbappe and me, we're the two best players in the world," the 19-year-old Barcelona winger said in an interview on Movistar Plus, excerpts of which were published on Sunday.

Barca star Yamal says will not beg for Ballon d'Or

"I honestly think that, as the best in the world, maybe there are two of us, and this year I would deserve it because of what I've won," he added.

Yamal helped Barcelona retain La Liga before becoming a world champion with Spain this summer, strengthening his claim for the game's most prestigious individual award.

He had struck a more measured tone at a press conference last Tuesday, saying he believed he had a chance after an "incredible" season but would not beg for votes.

Mbappe embraces Ballon d'Or talk after historic World Cup exploits

Mbappe, meanwhile, has also made his case for the award in recent days.

The France captain finished as top scorer in La Liga, the Champions League and the World Cup, although Real Madrid failed to win a major trophy.

Yamal's Barcelona and Spain teammate Ousmane Dembele, last year's winner, believes the award should remain with a Paris Saint-Germain player after the French club retained the Champions League.

Bayern Munich striker and England international Harry Kane is also among the favourites to win the award, which will be issued in London on 26 October.

item.title: The digital lifeline must not be left to chance
item.description:
Internet access has evolved from being a luxury to becoming the very backbone of modern society. Today, a person might willingly skip a meal, but the thought of losing an internet connection for even a moment is met with panic. It is no longer just about entertainment or social media; it is about livelihood, education, healthcare, and commerce. It is the pulse of the nation’s economy.

This reality makes the current debate regarding Bangladesh’s future international bandwidth supply a matter of critical national security. We have a situation where private sector stakeholders are sounding alarm bells, projecting a severe capacity crunch as early as 2028, while the state-owned monopoly, Bangladesh Submarine Cable Company PLC (BSCPLC), dismisses these fears as "misleading and divorced from reality."

When the state’s official machinery and the private sector offer completely opposite versions of the future, it creates a fog of uncertainty. However, given the high stakes, the government cannot afford to sit back and assume the state agency is correct simply because it is the state. A neutral, thorough, and independent assessment is required immediately. The cost of being wrong is simply too high.

The numbers presented by the private sector are not random guesses; they are projections based on explosive growth. In 2013, the country used just 50 Gbps. By 2026, that number has exploded to 13.5 Tbps. That is a 260-fold increase in thirteen years. The forecast suggests a demand for nearly 27 Tbps by 2028 and up to 54 Tbps by 2030. While BSCPLC counters by citing its existing unused capacity and the upcoming SEA-ME-WE 6 cable, the core issue is about time, redundancy, and the fragility of relying on a single supplier.

We must look at this issue not from the perspective of corporate profits or state-entity pride, but from the perspective of national resilience. The first point of concern is the geography of our connectivity. Bangladesh, a nation of 170 million people driving a rapidly digitizing economy, relies primarily on only two submarine cables: SEA-ME-WE-4 and SEA-ME-WE-5. To put this in perspective, India is connected to 19 cables, Malaysia to 23, and the Philippines to 19. This disparity is alarming.

Submarine cables are prone to faults—whether from underwater earthquakes, dragging ship anchors, or technical failures. If one of Bangladesh's two aging cables suffers a major fault, the other alone cannot sustain the current demand, let alone future growth.

We saw the panic that ensued in other regions when cables were severed; for a nation so dependent on the internet, a lack of redundancy is a gamble with the national economy. BSCPLC assures us that SEA-ME-WE-6 will solve the problem by adding 34,000 Gbps of capacity by 2027.

While this is a welcome development, it still does not erase the vulnerability of having a "single point of failure" in the overall architecture. Furthermore, SEA-ME-WE-4 is scheduled to be decommissioned by 2030. This means that by the time we think we have solved the crisis, we will be retiring the very infrastructure that currently holds us together. The second concern is the bottleneck of bureaucracy.

The private consortium warns that planning, financing, and constructing a submarine cable takes years. If we wait until 2027 to see if the demand matches the supply, we have already lost. If the private sector is wrong and BSCPLC is right, we lose nothing by approving private cable projects now. However, if the private sector is right and BSCPLC is wrong, the country descends into a digital dark age characterised by slow speeds, high costs, and economic stagnation.

There is a suspicion in some quarters that the private investors are merely lobbying for their own financial interests. That may be true. They are businesses, after all, and they seek profit. However, their profit motive does not invalidate their data. The government should not reject a solution simply because a private company will make money from it. We do not ask private power producers to operate for free; we welcome their investment to solve the electricity crisis. Why should the internet be any different?

Allowing private submarine cables is not a concession to corporate greed; it is a strategy to diversify risk. Competition in the international bandwidth market would lower prices for consumers and create a safety net. Currently, the country is heavily reliant on BSCPLC and a few International Terrestrial Cable (ITC) operators. If BSCPLC faces technical or financial difficulties, the nation suffers. A diversified portfolio, including privately owned cables, would make the internet ecosystem more robust.
BSCPLC’s rebuttal pointed to "unused capacity" of 3,200 Gbps.

However, looking at the trend of the last decade, that buffer will be consumed rapidly. The government''s own plan to bring 7 crore feature-phone users under mobile data services within the next year will consume a massive chunk of that "spare" capacity. We are talking about adding tens of millions of new users to the network. When that happens, the demand curve will not be linear; it will be exponential. This brings us to a more profound issue: trust and accountability.

Too often, state entities deny problems until they become unmanageable, before finally admitting the crisis. We saw this pattern in the banking sector and the energy sector. The public was reassured for years that everything was fine, only to be hit by crippling crises later. The current government is well aware of the political volatility of internet shutdowns.
The previous government’s decision to shut down the internet resulted in massive economic losses and a severe blow to its legitimacy.

The public can tolerate load shedding of electricity, they complain, but they cope. They cannot and will not tolerate an internet crisis. If the country descends into a bandwidth shortage in 2028 or 2029, the anger will not be directed at undersea cables or technical faults; it will be directed at the government.

Therefore, a humble plea to the authorities is to treat this not as a technical issue for the telecom ministry, but as a sovereign issue. It is a matter of "digital sovereignty." We cannot allow our digital future to be decided solely by a single state-owned company that has a vested interest in maintaining its monopoly. An independent audit of the bandwidth demand projections is necessary. The Prime Minister’s Office should convene a high-level meeting involving BTRC, BSCPLC, the private consortium, and independent international consultants.

The goal should not be to prove who is right, but to find out what is true. The digital highway is as critical to Bangladesh as its physical roads and bridges. We would not leave the construction of a major bridge solely to a single company without scrutiny.

The internet is the bridge to the global economy. It is time to set aside the ego of state agencies and the suspicions regarding private investors. It is time to plan for the worst, hope for the best, and build a network that can sustain the dreams of Bangladesh digitally. The time to act is now. If we wait for the crisis to arrive, it will be too late to build the ship.

* Naim-Ul-Karim Sanchaya, Special correspondent & in-charge at Xinhua News Agency’s Dhaka Bureau office.
